carnage.name: GimmeG
carnage.commentary: The damage was a 6 on the 5th: a par-3 that turned into a net-and-gross double-hit to the jaw, and he never really unclenched after that.

carnage.name: Scottiet
carnage.commentary: The ugly one came at the 5th, where a par-3 became a 5 and left a little extra soot on the card.

carnage.name: StevieD
carnage.commentary: The 4th was the brick wall: par-3, 5 on the card, and a momentum leak he never fully patched up.

carnage.name: bkane
carnage.commentary: It started ugly on the 1st, a par-3 stuffed with a 4 and an early blemish before the putter tried to bail everything out.

carnage.name: crzygoalie
carnage.commentary: The 5th was the blemish: par-3, 4 on the card, and just enough slop to keep the line from getting cleaner.

carnage.name: llyreks
carnage.commentary: The 5th was the worst of it, a par-3 turned into a 4 and the kind of cheap bogey that keeps the round from really taking off.

players.name: Scottiet
players.tagline: A pile of short-game duct tape with one big putting leak.
players.body: Scottiet landed in 13th net, but the card underneath was a weird little science experiment: even on the week, 26th gross, with the game dragged around by a putting mess that cost him 1.28 strokes and a total of 27 putts. The saving grace was the chipping, because +4.53 around the greens is absurdly clean and the best number on the profile; he also scraped out 4-for-4 in sand and finished at +1.50 total despite losing 1.75 on approach. The hole-by-hole shape is blunt: a bogey on the 5th was the worst of it, but the round also had actual juice with birdies on the 6th and 7th and another edge at the 17th. Still, 9 GIR and 2 three-putts is not exactly trophy-level plumbing. No prior starts here, so there’s no trend to pretend exists; this was just one round where the short game did a lot of the heavy lifting while the approach and putter took turns being annoying.

players.name: StevieD
players.tagline: A putter fire drill that somehow still didn’t burn the whole house down.
players.body: StevieD finished 14th net and 37th gross, which is what happens when you keep enough things barely afloat to avoid total disaster but the putter goes full sabotage mode. He gave back 2.97 strokes putting, made only 45 feet of putts compared with a 65-foot peer number, and still managed to stay within shouting distance because the tee-to-green piece was decent at +1.47 and the short game chipped in +2.23. The rest of the card was messy but not apocalyptic: 8 GIR, 26 putts, one three-putt, and four bogeys against three birdies plus one double-or-worse. His worst hole was the 4th, a par-3 he played in 5, and that was very much the vibe all day — too many small leaks, not enough made putts to patch them. With no prior starts to compare against, this is just the raw profile: some competence tee to green, a whole lot of pain on the greens, and a scorecard that got mugged by basic math.

players.name: GimmeG
players.tagline: Birdie machine with a sand wedge that wandered off for a smoke break.
players.body: GimmeG checked in 15th net, with a gross line of 28th that says the ball-striking was fine but the scoring math never really cleaned itself up. The weird part is the profile: +0.50 total with 11 GIR and seven birdies, so there was plenty of productive golf in there, but 27 putts and 0-for-3 from the sand kept the round from turning into anything sharper. Approach was basically flat at +0.20, putting was a small plus at +0.35, and the short game was close to neutral at -0.05, which is a fancy way of saying nothing got wildly broken or wildly fixed. The 5th hole was the worst of the damage, a par-3 doubled into a 6, and he also coughed up another ugly one at the 10th with a 5. Still, this wasn’t a dead round — four birdies is a real output, and the GIR number was actually strong relative to peers. No history yet, so the only honest read is that this was a playable but messy first look, with enough greens and birdies to matter and enough sand/putting leakage to keep him off the podium.

players.name: crzygoalie
players.tagline: The kind of round that keeps you in it while your scorecard gets quietly shredded in gross.
players.body: crzygoalie finished 16th net, but the gross result was 18th and the underlying numbers are the sneaky part: +3.50 total and +4.15 tee to green is a legit teeth-filing performance, especially with +3.37 around the greens and 11 GIR on the card. He only made four birdies, but he also held the doubles to zero and avoided a three-putt entirely, which is how you end up with a round that looks sturdier than the net placement suggests. The bad hole was the 5th, where a par-3 became a 4, and there was another 4 on the 10th, but the rest of the round was mostly controlled noise rather than full-blown carnage. The weird split is obvious: he was much better gross than net suggests, yet the net finish didn’t reward it because the field was making him work for every little scrap. With no prior starts, there’s no pattern to overread; this was simply a pretty solid raw-golf round that didn’t cash in enough in the net race.

players.name: bkane
players.tagline: The putter was hot enough to hide the rest of the mess for a while.
players.body: bkane landed 17th net, but gross 15th tells the real story: the ball was moving, the putter was cooking, and the round still found a way to leak enough blood to keep it from becoming a real score. He posted +5.50 total with a ridiculous +3.37 putting and +2.76 on approach, plus 13 GIR and 82 feet of putts made, which is exactly the kind of line that should scare people. The problem was the rest of the plumbing: four bogeys, one double-or-worse, and a first-hole par-3 that opened with a bogey right away. After that, he did rack up birdies in bunches, but the short game was negative and the front-end damage kept the finish from matching the quality of the raw strokes gained. This is also a clean first data point — no prior starts, no trend to hide behind — but the raw profile is obvious: if the approach stays that sharp and the putter doesn’t cool off, there’s a much nastier round in here than the net result showed.

players.name: llyreks
players.tagline: Enough recovery shots to survive, not enough birdie juice to scare anybody.
players.body: llyreks closed 18th net, with a gross tie at 24th, and the card reads like a round that spent too much time cleaning up instead of attacking. He actually won a little on the tee-to-green side at +0.94 and got +1.63 from the short game, but the approach work was a drag at -0.68 and the birdie total never really showed up — just two on the day. The defense was decent: 3-for-4 in sand, only two bogeys, and no double-or-worse, which kept the round from getting uglier than it had to be. Still, 8 GIR and 26 putts don’t exactly scream “dangerous,” and the 5th hole was the worst look, a par-3 that turned into a 4. There was also a late little punch with a birdie on 18, but by then the round had already settled into its shape. Like the rest of this batch, there’s no prior history to work from, so the honest read is simple: respectable rescue work, not enough clean offense, and a scorecard that needed more firepower than it got.
